CLI.doc:
The runner's command line (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D19):

- `list [FILTER]`: the tests, with their tags, and nothing run;
- `run [FILTER] [--tier T] [-j N] [--mem MB] [--keep] [--failed]`: the
  tests the filter selects (and the tier, a tag), on `N` processors
  (by default those of the machine less its load from outside) and `MB`
  megabytes; `--failed` runs the tests that failed last time,
  `--keep` keeps every test's directory, and `--accept` writes what the
  tests printed into their golden files (`Run.accept`);
- `explain PATH`: a test's command, directory and needs;
- `stats`: the slowest and the flakiest tests in the history;
- `doctor [FILTER]`: the capabilities the tests require, each probed,
  with how to get those that are missing (it fails when one is).

A run of the tier check, or with `--strict`, fails a test whose
capability is missing; any other run skips it. For flaky tests
(docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D17): `--repeat N` runs the selection N
times, `--until-fail` until a run fails (at most N times, 100 by
default), and `--under-load` keeps every processor busy beside it.

A filter is the language of `TestFilter`; two or more of them select
the tests any of them selects. The tests a selected test waits for are
selected with it, and a run runs the tests tagged `always` as well.
`--profile P` is `--tier P`.

`--affected` keeps, of what is selected, the tests that cover a path
changed since `HEAD` (in the work tree, or not yet known to git);
`--since REV` since `REV`, and `--changed FILE` the paths that `FILE`
lists, one to a line. A test covers the paths its tags `covers:GLOB`
match; a changed path that no test covers keeps every test. `--root DIR` is the directory of the tree (default `.`), `--out DIR` where
runs go (default `tests/out/r`), `--history FILE` the history (default
`build/test-history.tsv`). A run ends the program with success when every
test passed, with failure otherwise, and with 2 for a mistake in the
command line.

members.name: main
members.spec: val main : Run.command Test.tree -> unit
members.doc: `main tests` runs the command line's command over `tests`.

members.name: mainWith
members.spec: val mainWith : {tests : Run.command Test.tree, capabilities : Requirements.capability list, quarantine : string} -> unit
members.doc:
`mainWith {tests, capabilities, quarantine}` is `main tests`, with
what the tests may require and what is in quarantine.

`capabilities` are what tests may require (`Requirements`), and
`quarantine` the file of the quarantine's expectations ("" for none).

EXPECTATIONS.doc:
What a suite expects of its tests in some ways (docs/plans/unit-testing.md,
D16; docs/testing.md, Expectations): one format, and one meaning for
each category, for every list of deviations and skips.

A file has a line for each expectation, and `#` begins a comment:

```sml
WAY-GLOB | PATH-GLOB[::LABEL-GLOB] | CATEGORY | reason
```

The globs have `*` (any run of characters), `?` (one character) and
`[...]` (one of the characters, or ranges such as `0-9`, that it holds;
`[!...]` one that it does not), as the shell has them, and must match the
whole way, path or label. A line of three fields,
`PATH-GLOB | CATEGORY | reason`, is of every way. A category's meaning is one of
four:

- strict: the test must fail where the line says (`RUNE-DEV`, `HOST-BUG`,
  `WIDTH`, `SPEC-AMBIGUOUS`, `WINDOWS`, `EMULATED`, `FAILS`). A test that
  passes there fails, and a line that matches no failure in a way that
  ran is stale;
- lenient: the test may pass or fail (`HOST-FLAKY`, `FLAKY`);
- skip: the test is not run, for the reason given (`HOST-ABSENT`,
  `XC1-NA`, `XC2-NA`, `UNTESTED`, `UNSUPPORTED`). A line that names no
  test is stale;
- quarantine: the test runs and is reported, and its failure fails
  nothing until the date the reason begins with (`QUARANTINE`, with
  `until YYYY-MM-DD:`); after it the line is stale.

members.name: meaning
members.spec: datatype meaning = Strict | Lenient | Skip | Quarantine
members.doc: What a category means.

members.name: line
members.spec:
type line = {file : string, number : int, way : string, path : string, label : string option,
             category : string, reason : string}
members.doc: A line: where it is, its globs, its category and its reason.

members.name: Parse
members.spec: exception Parse of string
members.doc:
Raised by `parse` for a line that is not an expectation, with its file
and number.

members.name: meaning
members.spec: val meaning : string -> meaning option
members.doc:
`meaning c` is what the category `c` means, or `NONE` for no category.

**Example** `meaning "HOST-BUG" = SOME Strict`

members.name: parse
members.spec: val parse : string * string -> line list
members.doc:
`parse (file, text)` is the lines of `text`, the contents of `file`.

**Raises** `Parse` for a line with too few fields or a category that is
not one, or a quarantine without its date.

**Example** `length (parse ("f", "# a comment\n* | a/* | FLAKY | why\n")) = 1`

members.name: read
members.spec: val read : string -> line list
members.doc: `read file` is the lines of `file`, or none when there is no file.

members.name: glob
members.spec: val glob : string * string -> bool
members.doc:
`glob (g, s)` says whether the glob `g` matches the whole of `s`.

**Example** `glob ("lang/*/rt.?", "lang/native/rt.a")`

**Example** `glob ("*.scan/DEC-[avfr]*", "Int.scan/DEC-v1") andalso not (glob ("[!o]x", "ox"))`

members.name: find
members.spec: val find : line list * {way : string, path : string, label : string option} -> line option
members.doc:
`find (ls, {way, path, label})` is the first line of `ls` that matches
the test, if any.

A line with a label matches only that test's label; one without
matches the test, whatever its label.

members.name: skipped
members.spec: val skipped : line list * {way : string, path : string} -> line option
members.doc:
`skipped (ls, {way, path})` is the line that skips the test of `path`
in `way`, if one does.

members.name: outcome
members.spec:
datatype outcome = Pass | Fail | Expected of line | Unexpected of line | Flaky of line
                 | Quarantined of line | Expired of line
members.doc:
What a test that ran comes to, given the lines.

`Pass` and `Fail` where no line speaks; `Expected` for a strict line's
failure, and `Unexpected` for its pass; `Flaky` for a lenient line;
`Quarantined` for a quarantined failure before its date, and `Expired`
for one after it.

members.name: judge
members.spec:
val judge : line list * {way : string, path : string, label : string option, passed : bool, today : string}
            -> outcome
members.doc:
`judge (ls, {way, path, label, passed, today})` is what the test comes
to; `today` is the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

members.name: failing
members.spec: val failing : outcome -> bool
members.doc:
`failing oc` says whether `oc` fails the run.

**Example** `failing Fail andalso not (failing Pass)`

members.name: stale
members.spec: val stale : line list * {ways : string list, paths : string list, used : line list, today : string} -> line list
members.doc:
`stale (ls, {ways, paths, used, today})` is the lines of `ls` that are
stale after a run.

Those are a strict line that names a way in `ways` and is not in
`used` (the lines of the failures it expected), a skip line whose path
matches none of `paths`, and a quarantine past its date.

members.name: describe
members.spec: val describe : line -> string
members.doc: `describe l` is `l` as its file and number say it, for a report.

HISTORY.doc:
What earlier runs found (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D13): per test, the
last wall times, the last outcome and how often it flipped, in a table of
tab-separated lines that each run rewrites. A fresh tree reads a seed
instead, which only a run of every test may write, since a test missing
from it would look cheap (HOL4's rule).

members.name: entry
members.spec: type entry = {path : string, walls : real list, passed : bool, flips : int}
members.doc:
A test's record: its path, its last wall times, its last verdict and
how often its verdict changed.

The wall times are in seconds, newest first, at most five; `flips`
counts the runs whose verdict was not the one before.

members.name: history
members.spec: type history
members.doc: A history: the records of the tests, by path.

members.name: empty
members.spec: val empty : history
members.doc:
The empty history.

**Example** `not (isSome (cost (empty, "any")))`

members.name: read
members.spec: val read : string -> history
members.doc: `read file` is the history in `file`, or `empty` when there is none.

members.name: write
members.spec: val write : string * history -> unit
members.doc: `write (file, h)` writes `h` to `file`, replacing it.

members.name: record
members.spec: val record : history * {path : string, wall : real, passed : bool} -> history
members.doc:
`record (h, {path, wall, passed})` is `h` with the run of a test
added: its wall time first among its five, and its flips counted.

**Example** `Real.== (valOf (cost (record (empty, {path = "t", wall = 2.0, passed = true}), "t")), 2.0)`

members.name: cost
members.spec: val cost : history * string -> real option
members.doc:
`cost (h, path)` is what the test of `path` is expected to take: the
longest of its last wall times, or `NONE` for a test never run.

members.name: failedLast
members.spec: val failedLast : history * string -> bool
members.doc:
`failedLast (h, path)` says whether the test of `path` failed the last
time it ran.

**Example** `failedLast (record (empty, {path = "t", wall = 1.0, passed = false}), "t") = true`

members.name: entries
members.spec: val entries : history -> entry list
members.doc: `entries h` is every record of `h`, by path.

REPORT.doc:
What a run says, to the reader it has (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D14).

On a terminal: one status line, redrawn at most ten times a second, with
each failure printed above it as it happens and a summary at the end. To
a log, and to an agent: nothing for a test that passes, a line every 30
seconds that says how far the run is, a block for each failure that
stands alone, and the summary. An agent, recognised by its environment
(`AI_AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CURSOR_AGENT`,
`GEMINI_CLI`), gets the path of the run's events at the start as well,
since it may see only the head and the tail of a long output. Every
failure line begins with its verdict, and the last line with `RESULT:`.
The run's events go to a file of JSON lines in every case, and the
summary, in Markdown, to the file summary.md beside it, and to the file
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` names when it names one.

members.name: reader
members.spec: datatype reader = Terminal | Log | Agent
members.doc: Who reads: a person at a terminal, a log, or an agent.

members.name: reader
members.spec: val reader : unit -> reader
members.doc:
`reader ()` is the reader of standard output: an agent when the
environment names one, a terminal when standard output is one, and a
log otherwise.

members.name: report
members.spec: type report
members.doc: A report being written.

members.name: start
members.spec: val start : {reader : reader, events : string, total : int} -> report
members.doc:
`start {reader, events, total}` begins the report of a run of `total`
tests, its events written to the file `events`.

members.name: tick
members.spec: val tick : report * int -> unit
members.doc:
`tick (r, running)` redraws the status line, or writes the line that
says the run goes on, when it is time to.

members.name: ended
members.doc:
What a test ended with: its path, its verdict and why, what it cost,
where its outputs are kept, and the command that reruns it.

The verdict is one of `PASS`, `FAIL`, `TIMEOUT`, `CRASH`, `LEAK`,
`ERROR`, `SKIP`, `ACCEPTED` (a golden file written, `Run.accept`),
`FLAKY` (a failure, then a pass) and `QUARANTINED`; the first, `SKIP`
and the last three are not failures.

members.name: test
members.spec: val test : report * ended -> unit
members.doc:
`test (r, e)` reports `e`: a failure as a block, a skip as a line with
its reason, a pass as a count, and each as an event.

members.name: finish
members.spec: val finish : report * {cpus : int, freed : int, keptBytes : int} -> bool
members.doc:
`finish (r, {cpus, freed, keptBytes})` writes the summary and the
`RESULT:` line, and is whether every test ran and passed.

`cpus` is the processors the run had, and `freed` and `keptBytes` the
bytes of output removed and kept.

REQUIREMENTS.doc:
What a test needs of the machine (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D18): a
capability is a name, a probe and an install hint. A test names the
capabilities it needs (`Test.requires`); the runner probes each once, and
a test whose capability is missing is skipped with the hint, or fails in
a run that must be complete, as the tier check is.

RUNE\_TEST\_WITHOUT names capabilities to take as missing, separated by
commas, so that what a machine without them gets can be seen on one
that has them.

members.name: capability
members.spec: type capability = {name : string, probe : string, hint : string}
members.doc:
A capability: its name, a command of the shell that exits with 0 when
it is there, and how to get it.

members.name: present
members.spec: val present : capability list * string -> bool
members.doc:
`present (cs, name)` says whether the capability `name` of `cs` is
there, probing it once; one that `cs` does not name is not.

members.name: missing
members.spec: val missing : capability list * string list -> (string * string) list
members.doc:
`missing (cs, names)` is the capabilities among `names` that are not
there, each with its hint.

RUN.doc:
A run of tests that are commands (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, M3): each
in a directory of its own of a fixed width under the run's directory, or
in a directory it names; judged when it ends; its directory removed when
it passed and kept when it did not; its wall time recorded in the
history; and every outcome reported.

members.name: command
members.spec:
type command = {program : string, args : string list, env : string list option, dir : string option,
                stdin : string option, timeout : Time.time, cap : int, cpus : int, memory : int,
                pools : string list, exclusive : bool, after : string list,
                judge : Supervisor.result * {stdout : string, stderr : string} -> (string * string) option}
members.doc:
A test that is a command: what runs, where, what it may take, what it
waits for, and how its verdict is found.

`after` names the tests it waits for by path. `judge` finds the
verdict from how the command ended and the files of its output and
errors: `NONE` passes, and `SOME (verdict, reason)` does not. `dir` is
`NONE` for a directory of its own. `env` is `NONE` for the runner's
environment without what would make a `make` inside it a part of the
runner's own (`MAKELEVEL`, `MFLAGS`, and the jobs and jobserver of
`MAKEFLAGS`, whose variables stay) or force colour (`FORCE_COLOR`,
`CLICOLOR_FORCE`). A command takes no more CPUs than the run has, and
finds how many it has in `RUNE_TEST_CPUS`, the run's directory in
`RUNE_TEST_RUN` and the tree's in `RUNE_TEST_ROOT`, both absolute;
`RUNE_TEST_ACCEPT` is 1 in a run that accepts (`accept`).

members.name: exitZero
members.spec: val exitZero : Supervisor.result * {stdout : string, stderr : string} -> (string * string) option
members.doc:
`exitZero (r, files)` is the verdict of a command that passes when it
exits with 0.

Otherwise its verdict is `FAIL`, `TIMEOUT`, `CRASH` (a signal) or
`LEAK` (it left processes behind), with the end of its output.

members.name: shell
members.spec: val shell : string * int -> command
members.doc:
`shell (script, cpus)` is a command that runs `script` with `/bin/sh -c`
in the directory of the tree, judged by `exitZero`.

Its timeout is an hour, and its output has no cap.

members.name: index
members.spec: val index : string vector -> string -> int option
members.doc:
`index names` finds a name among `names`: its place, or `NONE`.

**Example** `index (Vector.fromList ["b", "a"]) "a" = SOME 1`

members.name: tail
members.spec: val tail : int * string -> string
members.doc:
`tail (n, file)` is the last `n` lines of `file`, or "" when there is
none.

members.name: accept
members.spec: val accept : bool ref
members.doc:
Whether the run accepts what its tests printed as what they should
print (`--accept`).

A judge that reads a golden file writes it instead, and says
`ACCEPTED`. It is `false` unless the command line sets it.

members.name: run
members.spec:
val run : {tests : (string * Test.meta * command) list, root : string, out : string, history : string,
           cpus : int, memory : int, keep : bool, reader : Report.reader,
           capabilities : Requirements.capability list, strict : bool, quarantine : Expectations.line list} -> bool
members.doc:
`run {tests, root, out, history, cpus, memory, keep, reader, capabilities, strict, quarantine}` runs `tests` under `out`, and is
whether every test passed.

Each run has a new directory under `out`.

The tree's directory is `root`; the run has `cpus` processors and
`memory` megabytes; it reads and rewrites the history file `history`;
and `keep` keeps every test's directory. A test that requires a
capability the machine lacks (of `capabilities`) does not run: it is
skipped with the capability's hint, or is an ERROR when `strict`, and
the tests that wait for it do not start.

A test tagged `flaky` that fails runs once more, and is `FLAKY` (no
failure) when it passes then. A failure that a line of `quarantine`
covers, of the way `rune-test` and the test's path, is `QUARANTINED`
until the line's date, and a failure again after it.

SCHEDULER.doc:
Which jobs to start (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D12): the jobs of a run,
what has ended and what is free decide it, so that it can be tested on a
simulated clock.

A job takes CPUs and megabytes of memory while it runs, may hold named
pools (mutexes: two jobs that name one never overlap), may be exclusive
(it runs alone), and may wait for other jobs. Its priority is the critical
path: the longest chain of costs from it to the end of the run, so that
among jobs with no edges the longest starts first (Graham's LPT). A job
that failed last time starts before any other. An exclusive job that is
next lets the running jobs drain, and nothing starts in front of it.

A run's state is kept as it goes, so that a run of thousands of jobs costs
little at each start and end: the jobs each waits for are counted down,
and the jobs that may start are kept in the order of their priorities.

members.name: job
members.spec:
type job = {cost : real, cpus : int, memory : int, pools : string list, exclusive : bool,
            failedLast : bool, deps : int list}
members.doc:
A job as the scheduler sees it: its cost, what it takes and holds, and
the jobs it waits for.

The cost is in seconds, from the history. `deps` are the indices of
the jobs it waits for; `exclusive` runs it alone.

members.name: plan
members.spec: type plan
members.doc: A run's plan: the jobs and their priorities.

members.name: plan
members.spec: val plan : job vector -> plan
members.doc:
`plan jobs` is the plan of `jobs`, numbered by their places.

**Raises** `Fail` if a job waits for itself, or for one that waits for
it, or for no job.

members.name: priority
members.spec: val priority : plan * int -> real
members.doc:
`priority (p, i)` is job `i`'s priority: its cost and the longest chain
of costs after it, and more than every other for a job that failed
last time.

**Example** `Real.== (priority (plan (Vector.fromList [{cost = 2.0, cpus = 1, memory = 0, pools = [], exclusive = false, failedLast = false, deps = []}]), 0), 2.0)`

members.name: state
members.spec: type state
members.doc:
A run under way: which jobs wait, run and have ended, and what the
running ones take.

members.name: start
members.spec: val start : plan -> state
members.doc: `start p` is the state of a run of `p` before any job has started.

members.name: admit
members.spec: val admit : state * {cpus : int, memory : int} -> int list
members.doc:
`admit (s, {cpus, memory})` is the jobs to start now, the highest
priority first, on a machine of `cpus` and `memory`; they are running
from then on.

A job may start once every job it waits for has ended well, when it
fits what the running jobs leave free, and when no running job holds a
pool of its. A job that takes more than the machine has starts alone
when nothing runs, so that no job waits forever.

members.name: ended
members.spec: val ended : state * int * bool -> int list
members.doc:
`ended (s, i, ok)` records that job `i` ended, well when `ok`, and is
the jobs that will now never start.

Those are the jobs that wait, directly or not, for a job that did not
end well.

members.name: retry
members.spec: val retry : state * int -> unit
members.doc:
`retry (s, i)` puts the running job `i` back among those that may
start, as if it had not run.

members.name: finished
members.spec: val finished : state -> bool
members.doc: `finished s` says whether no job waits or runs.

members.name: simulate
members.spec: val simulate : plan * {cpus : int, memory : int} -> real vector * real
members.doc:
`simulate (p, {cpus, memory})` is when each job would start, and the
makespan, in the schedule `admit` makes.

The machine has `cpus` and `memory`, and each job takes its cost.

**Example** `Real.== (#2 (simulate (plan (Vector.fromList [{cost = 1.0, cpus = 1, memory = 0, pools = [], exclusive = false, failedLast = false, deps = []}]), {cpus = 4, memory = 100})), 1.0)`

SUPERVISOR.doc:
Running jobs as children (docs/plans/unit-testing.md, D9 and D11): one
loop that starts what the scheduler admits, reaps what ended, ends what
ran too long or wrote too much, and sleeps a little when nothing
happened. There are no threads and no handlers of signals but the
interrupt, so this loop is the runner.

A job is a process in a process group of its own (a job on Windows), with
its standard input from a file and its output and errors to files, which
a crash leaves on disk; its signals start at their default actions. A
job that runs past its time is sent TERM, and KILL after a grace period;
one whose output passes its cap is stopped by its file-size limit and by
the loop, which looks at the files' sizes. When the job's process has
ended and its group has not, the rest of the group is killed and the job
is said to have left processes behind.

members.name: command
members.spec:
type command = {program : string, args : string list, env : string list, dir : string,
                stdin : string, stdout : string, stderr : string, timeout : Time.time, cap : int,
                cost : real, cpus : int, memory : int, pools : string list, exclusive : bool,
                failedLast : bool, deps : int list}
members.doc:
A command to run: the program and its arguments, its environment and
directory, the files of its streams, its time and cap, and what it takes.

The arguments begin with the program's name. `cap` limits the bytes of
its output and errors, and of any file it writes (0 for none). The
rest is what the scheduler needs (`Scheduler.job`).

members.name: outcome
members.spec: datatype outcome = Exited of int | Signalled of int | TimedOut | Capped | Cancelled | Failed of string
members.doc:
How a command ended: its exit status or signal, ended by the loop, or
never started.

The loop ends a command for its time (`TimedOut`) or its output
(`Capped`). A command is `Cancelled` when a job it waited for did not
end well, and `Failed` when the system refused to start it.

members.name: verdict
members.spec: datatype verdict = Passed | NotPassed | Again
members.doc:
What a command came to: it passed, it did not, or it is to run again
(a test that may be flaky, the first time it fails).

members.name: result
members.spec:
type result = {outcome : outcome, wall : Time.time, user : Time.time, system : Time.time,
               peakResident : int, outputBytes : int, leaked : bool}
members.doc:
What a command cost: its times, its memory and its output, and whether
it left processes behind.

The wall time is on the monotonic clock; `peakResident` is the most
memory it held resident, in kilobytes.

members.name: outcomeName
members.spec: val outcomeName : outcome -> string
members.doc:
`outcomeName oc` is `oc` as a word or two, for a report.

**Example** `outcomeName (Exited 3) = "exit 3"`

members.name: run
members.spec:
val run : {commands : command vector, cpus : int, memory : int,
           finished : int * result -> verdict, tick : int -> unit} -> unit
members.doc:
`run {commands, cpus, memory, finished, tick}` runs `commands` as
`Scheduler.admit` admits them, and tells `finished` each one's result.

The machine has `cpus` processors and `memory` megabytes. `tick` is
called with the number running whenever the loop has nothing to do,
for a display.

`finished` says what the command came to; one to run `Again` is
started again. A command that waits for one that did not pass is not
started, and is `Cancelled`. An interrupt (`SML90.Interrupt`) kills every
running group and is raised again.
